Attachments: I attached a copy of our standard data retention policy (redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf) and a proposed exception template (proposed-retention-exception.xlsx) to help speed the review.

2) Legal draft of a short addendum for the retention exception (if doable) — I can loop in legal once SE confirms feasibility.
3) Security/Compliance to review export capabilities and attestations (Emily to share security@fintechco.com).

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed; a few clarifications below from the security side: 

- Embeddings: yes, we need embeddings derived from PII to be treated as PII (so covered by the 0-retention ask).
- Billing metadata: 24h retention for tokens/usage is acceptable as long as payloads are not retained. Can you confirm whether we can redact PII from logs before any snapshotting/backups?
- Audit logs: security@fintechco.com would like the ability to request an export (for a given time window) of request/response metadata and routing logs — acceptable if payloads are redacted.

We will need an attestation or process that confirms deletion once the exception is in effect. Also, does Redwood provide a documented timeline for deletion (e.g., immediate purge vs. eventual background job)?

Please loop in your SE to confirm the technical approach and then we can get legal involved to draft the addendum. Happy to set a technical call this Thursday morning PST.

Camila / Vivek / Emily — thanks for the clear thread. Technical confirmation and proposed plan below.

Technical feasibility (hosted offering):
- Per-customer 0-retention: We can implement a tenant-level retention toggle that will stop persisting request/response bodies and embeddings to long-term storage and instead enqueue them for immediate truncation after inference. For hosted, this requires a short-lived feature flag and an immediate deletion job. We can deliver this as a gated change with the following constraints:
  - Deletion timeline: best-effort immediate purge; records may persist in ephemeral caches and ephemeral logs for up to 60 minutes before the truncation job runs. We can tighten this to <5 minutes for enterprise customers on a Dedicated plan.
  - Embeddings: supportable as 0-retention. If FinTechCo needs to re-use embeddings for downstream tasks, we recommend Dedicated or Private where customer can host embeddings.
- Shortened non-PII telemetry: We can set a 30-day retention policy for non-PII telemetry (routing, error traces, latency metrics). We will redact any fields identified as PII prior to storage.
- Audit exports: We can provide metadata/export of routing logs and anonymized request IDs on demand. For full forensic exports, we will provide a redacted export; payloads will be removed. Exports are produced as CSV/NDJSON and delivered via secure S3 presigned link.

Operational / legal notes:
- Finance/billing: we need a minimum of 24h of token-level metadata for accurate invoicing. We can flag records as anonymized for the tenant (remove text payloads), which should satisfy billing while aligning with the 0-retention ask.
- Attestation: Once exception is enabled we can provide a signed addendum from Legal confirming the retention schedule and deletion process.

Timeline / next steps:
1) Engineering (Vivek + infra) to scope feature-flag rollout and runbook — ETA: 10 business days to enable tenant-level truncation on hosted with 60-minute deletion window.
2) Legal to draft short addendum (Camila to loop Legal) — ETA: 3-5 business days after SE sign-off.
3) Security review: we will provide a sample redacted export and a description of the deletion pipeline for FinTechCo's review.

If FinTechCo requires stricter SLAs (e.g., <5-minute deletion window or on-prem/Private deployment), recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; I can prepare a short comparison doc.

Happy to jump on the Thursday technical call — Vivek, can you take the lead on the implementation plan?

Best,

Marissa Cole
